sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Cache name and offline address
sections.what: Sets the name of the cache and the address of the offline page.
sections.why: Likely reason: the name is changed when files need to be refreshed. Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: The cache name must be changed on each release, or users keep old files.

sections.name: ASSETS_TO_CACHE
sections.title: Pages cached at install
sections.what: Lists the pages and icons saved the first time the app is installed so they work offline.
sections.why: Stated implicitly by the offline goal. Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: The dashboard page is saved, so personal layout may be visible offline on a shared device.

sections.name: self install handler
sections.title: Install step saves the list
sections.what: On install, saves the listed files and takes over right away without waiting for old copies to close.
sections.why: Likely reason: so new versions take effect sooner. Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: Taking over early can switch a page that is already open to new code mid-use. If any listed file fails to download, the whole install fails.

sections.name: self activate handler
sections.title: Activate step removing old caches
sections.what: When a new version starts, deletes any cache whose name does not match the current one.
sections.why: Likely reason: prevents old files from filling storage or being served. Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: Depends on the cache name being changed for each release.

sections.name: self fetch handler
sections.title: Network and cache request handling
sections.what: Page visits try the network first and fall back to the offline page. Other requests check the cache first, and static or icon files are saved as they are fetched.
sections.why: Likely reason: fresh pages when online, fast files and offline use otherwise. Reason not fully stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: Cached files are returned before the network is tried, so a cached response can be out of date until the cache name changes.

sections.name: self push handler
sections.title: Push notification display
sections.what: When a push message arrives, shows a notification with a title, body and icon, and stores the link to open.
sections.why: The comment says it is for push notifications. Specific design reasons not stated.
sections.watch_out: If the message is not valid JSON, reading it fails and no notification is shown.

sections.name: self notificationclick handler
sections.title: Opening the link on notification click
sections.what: When the user taps a notification, closes it and opens the stored link in a window.
sections.why: Likely reason: takes the user straight to the relevant page. Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: The link is not checked, so a message carrying an outside address would open that address.

summary: A background script in the browser that caches pages for offline use, serves cached files when offline, and shows push notifications.
purpose: Lets the app open partly without a connection and show alerts from the server.
why: The header says offline resilience and background sync. Background sync is not implemented in the visible code.
how: On install, it saves a short list of pages and images and takes over right away. On activate, it deletes old caches. On each request, page visits try the network and fall back to an offline page, while other files come from the cache first. Push messages show notifications, and clicking one opens its link.
inputs: Browser requests, and push messages carrying a title, body and optional url.
outputs: Cached responses, offline pages, and notifications.
risks: The dashboard page is cached, so personal health layout may appear offline on a shared device. Push handling fails if the message is not JSON. Cached files only change when the cache name is changed.
debug: Use the browser developer tools Application tab to see caches and the worker. Clearing site data resets it. Check that the offline page exists, since it is not in the cache list.
